questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That Singapore is a place where many different people and cultures meet at one place. One og the biggest aspects was that it was a country where Chinese also was spoken.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite hard. There was send a lot of different emails with information, but due to covid they changed all the time. It was quite confusing

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a introduction for all exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The system of choosing courses was so confusing, and not friendly for exchange students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was mandatory to live on campus. We had to fill out a form before arriving with preferences for the living conditions/environment

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Only food in dining hall. However here was always a vegan option. If you wanted something else you could buy cheap food in U town.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You live together in either 4 or 6 people suites. It is either with full-time students at the university or other exchange students. It depends where there is space.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The full-time students I lived with was all seniors, so they was very busy and I did not spend much time with them do to this.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration and moving in was fine when you were there. Quite easy. However there was a lot of preparation beforehand.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We had a contact person which was happy to help us.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not that succesful. The system is really confusing. Besides that the classes I intentionally wanted was not offered, so it was a big puzzle in general.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't have to many expectations, and don't get stressed and disappointed if you don't get the classes you wanted in the first place. You just have to adapt to the situation

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of classes was not offered to exchange students. I think they could offer more.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is high. Be prepared for a lot of preparation.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much higher. It was hard to adjust to.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Advance Chinese 1, Beyond China: Sinophone literature, Cities Adelaide to Zhuhai, Political Economy in Capitalism.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Advance Chinese 1 and Cities A to Z. The Chinese teacher is so understanding and a great teacher. I learned a lot! Cities A to Z is a really interesting course which gives an insight in many different cities around the world and their urban planning.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There was some extra fees which we had to pay the school

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general I found Singapore less expensive than I imagined. Only eating out is around the same prices as in Denmark, unless you go to hawker center (which is really cheap). However flight tickets was quite expensive do to the situation of covid and that it had to be a VTL flight.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many opportunities and really an engaging community.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything from sports, to musical, to film club, board game night and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Board game nights, the different sport activities and just in general all the small events the community is holding.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go outside the campus! Regret not going out more. If the opportunity is there also go visit other places nearby like Malaysia, Indonesia etc. Quite sad that I didn't have this opportunity due to covid.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. I have been in Beijing before, so Singapore was not a culture chok for me.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs, and just be open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The different expectations for cleaning in the suite.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness of the people, and the food.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open, be prepared to study (a lot), but don't forget to relax and see other things!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The community is so unique, take advantage of the many activities there!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting some really nice people, and experiencing the culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The work load

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
